hints: Notice the diagram order along the 2.0 m pipe is N A N A N A N A, with N at the closed left end and A at the open right end.
Recall that the distance between an adjacent node and antinode in a stationary wave is one quarter of a wavelength, $\lambda/4$.
Count how many N-to-A or A-to-N gaps fit between the first N and the last A, then set that number times $\lambda/4$ equal to $2.0\text{ m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the ends from the diagram: the closed end is a displacement node N and the open end is a displacement antinode A, and the 2.0 m length runs from the first N to the last A.
State the stationary-wave rule: adjacent node to antinode separation is $\lambda/4$.
Count the adjacent gaps in N A N A N A N A: there are $7$ gaps in total between successive letters.
Set up the length equation: $7 \times \lambda/4 = 2.0\text{ m}$.
Solve: $\lambda = 4 \times 2.0/7 = 8.0/7 \approx 1.14\text{ m}$, which to two significant figures is about $1.1\text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$.
